summary: The note describes how community theater, exemplified by the Oakendale Playhouse, drives economic and cultural vitality in small towns. Since the playhouse reopened on September 5, 2023, nearby hospitality and retail businesses have seen more foot traffic and revenue, while an internship program and educational outreach nurture young talent. The piece also stresses theater's role in preserving local traditions and bringing generations together.
one_line: Community theater like the Oakendale Playhouse boosts local businesses, builds cultural bonds, and trains young talent in small towns.
key_facts: The Oakendale Playhouse reopened on September 5, 2023, after renovations to the historic building.
Since the reopening, local businesses, especially in hospitality and retail, have seen increased foot traffic and revenue that often aligns with the theater's performance schedule.
Cynthia Marlowe owns the 'Thespian's Nook', a boutique two blocks from the playhouse, and reported more customers seeking gifts and memorabilia, especially when 'The Glass Menagerie' was on.
Joseph Knapp, head chef and owner of the 'Apron & Artichoke' bistro, says patrons come early to secure parking and have dinner before shows.
Knapp has developed creative themed menus that coincide with different playhouse productions.
Barbara Jensen, a retired schoolteacher and loyal patron, says she has watched children grow from hesitant performers to confident adults on the playhouse stage.
The playhouse launched an internship program in October 2023, led by director Harold Green and educational coordinator Lisa Fontaine.
The internship invites high school students to take part in all aspects of theater production, including set design, lighting, and costume making.
Lisa Fontaine says the program instills 'a sense of craftsmanship and pride that translates to any future career.'
Some interns have contributed to the local economy by starting their own businesses or revitalizing existing ones.
Upcoming productions include classics like 'Our Town', which the note says give old tales new relevance.
The note argues that theater and commerce form an ecosystem in which culture and business thrive off one another, benefiting everyone from the teenager running lights to the seasoned actor.
